text:
incident-bot: PAGING: p99 end-to-end latency spike observed in eu-west (streaming endpoints). Auto-alert fired: p99 > 1200ms for last 3 minutes. Paging on-call.
Alex H: I’m on it, grabbing pager. Any customer-facing error spikes?
Tara C: CS telemetry shows increased client reconnects for two customers in EU, but no new error codes yet. They report stalls during long streams.
Priya S: Looking at metrics: streaming tail stalls correlate with spikes in connection handshake duration and TCP retransmits to nat-gw-eu-azb. p95 ~ 420ms -> p99 ~ 1.3s.
Alex H: Can you post the relevant dashboards?
Priya S: Dashboard snippets: 
```
metric: streaming.tail.latency.p99 = 1300ms
metric: tcp.retransmits/nat-gw-eu = +400% over baseline
metric: dns.lookup.err_rate = 0.8% -> spike
```
Mike N: I’m seeing elevated SYN->ESTABLISHED time on the path to NAT gateway, and conntrack table on the NAT instances is near 90% used. Possible ephemeral port churn.
eng-network: Packet captures show increased RSTs and some duplicate ACKs between az-b and az-c. Also noticed DNS timeouts around the same window.
Alex H: Could this be NAT ephemeral exhaustion or NAT gateway CPU/QPS saturation?
Mike N: Both plausible. NAT instance CPU trending up but not pegged. Conntrack and ephemeral port reuse look suspicious. Also some flows show multiple SYN retries -> handshake spikes.
Priya S: Impact summary: streaming endpoints degrade for sessions >30s, short requests mostly unaffected. Canary traffic to other region (eu-central) shows normal tail.
SRE Lead: Start mitigations: 1) shift streaming traffic away from eu-west2-azb to azc/aze if possible; 2) increase conntrack table and reuse timeouts; 3) failover DNS to healthy resolver.
Alex H: I can push a routing steering to prefer az-c for new sessions. Will do phased move.
Mike N: Before we steer, we should bump conntrack max on the NAT fleet and rotate one NAT instance (drain and replace) to free stateful entries. I'll run commands.
Priya S: Also enable temporary streaming-level retry/backoff to reduce handshake churn. Add a sliding-window limit on reconnect attempts from the client side (server-side proxy filter).
Alex H: Executing route steer now for ~10% of new sessions -> 50% -> 100%. Monitoring.
eng-network: After 10% shift, p99 dropped to 1.0s. After 50% it's 650ms. Good signal.
incident-bot: Action logged: traffic_steer/partial-rollout by Alex H at 5054322100.
Mike N: Increasing conntrack max and lowering timeout on NAT nodes. Commands: 
```
# on nat nodes
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300
```
Mike N: Triggering drain+replace for nat-gw-eu-azb-03 now.
eng-network: Drain started, connections being migrated. Observed a burst of retransmits during drain (~30s) but then stabilizes.
Priya S: After conntrack bump and replacement, p99 returned to ~480ms, p95 ~220ms. Streaming stalls reduced.
Tara C: Notifying affected customers: sent interim note to two impacted customers that we're mitigating and will follow up with RCA.
Alex H: Rolling the traffic steer to 100% complete. p99 stable at ~390-500ms. Keeping mitigations for 30m and will roll back if stable.
SRE Lead: Good. Next: preserve logs and packet captures (pcap) for root cause. Also open a full incident ticket for postmortem. Assigning to Priya + Mike.
Priya S: Collected pcaps, conntrack dumps, and NAT access logs. Key observations: sudden spike in short-lived flows from a subset of edge proxies -> likely client retry storm interacting with NAT ephemeral limits.
Mike N: Agreed. Also saw increased DNS lookup failures from internal resolver causing client libraries to retry and create new connections frequently. DNS secondary had higher latency.
Alex H: Temporary workaround for DNS: failover resolver to the internal resolver pool with healthy latency, and push DNS TTL lower for our service records to allow faster re-resolve to other AZs.
eng-network: Note: TLS handshake attempts per-second increased 6x during spike. Many handshakes timed out before completion. Possibly amplified by client-side reconnect loops.
Priya S: Customer impact: degraded streaming tail latency and intermittent stalls for long-running streams in eu-west for ~18 minutes. No data leakage or error codes. Post-incident mitigation reduced impact to negligible.
Tara C: CS follow-up: schedule 1:1 with customers to walk through timeline and ensure their client SDKs handle exponential backoff.
SRE Lead: Post-incident actions (short list):
- RCA: root causes (dns resolver latency + connection churn -> conntrack exhaustion + handshake retries).
- Mitigations: increase conntrack defaults, add autoscale triggers for NAT fleet, implement graceful drain patterns, health-check DNS resolvers, add RUM metrics for client retry rate.
- Follow-ups: eng-network to evaluate NAT gateway architecture (shared vs per-AZ) and consider per-AZ scaling or managed NAT with higher ephemeral pools.
Alex H: Creating incident ticket: INC-5054321987, assigning Priya and Mike. Will update with timeline and logs.
incident-bot: Incident INC-5054321987 created and paged on-call.
Priya S: Leaving monitoring on. Will post RCA draft in #postmortems in 24h.
Mike N: Adding playbook note: if conntrack > 85% and p99 > 700ms, start partial traffic steer and scale NAT pool.
Tara C: Thanks everyone. I'll update customers once RCA is ready. :thumbsup:
SRE Lead: Great job team. Keep the channel open until we close the ticket.
Alex H: Closing on-call shift in 30m unless new alerts.
eng-network: saved pcaps and logs to /var/logs/incidents/INC-5054321987/ (link: https://internal/redwood/logs/INC-5054321987).
incident-bot: Incident channel archived for follow-up when RCA posted.
